subject: Cloud interruption in EU/APAC — reassignment steps and next actions
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Cloud interruption in EU/APAC — immediate reassignment steps

Hi team —

Quick update from Redwood on the ongoing partition impacting our EU and APAC host pools (observed ~08:40 UTC): some front-line peering in the eu-west and apac-edge zones is flapping and causing elevated 503s and partial KV cache misses for traffic routed to those regions. US-hosted capacity is unaffected.

What we recommend right now to keep your production traffic healthy (minimal changes required):

1) Temporary regional override: set the X-Redwood-Region header to "us-west-2" on calls that require sub-100ms latency. This will route requests to our US pools while we stabilize EU/APAC. Example: curl -H "X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

2) SDK flag (client-side): use the force_region option in our SDK (v1.12+) — eg: client.setOption('force_region', 'us-west-2'). This will prefer US endpoints for new sessions.

3) Short-lived token refresh: if you rely on regional KMS-backed encryption keys, rotate session tokens to ensure no stale region-bound tokens remain. We attached an abbreviated command set for token refresh and a snapshot of the runbook we followed.

We will keep EU/APAC traffic in read-only routing to avoid writes that may trigger retries. Expect increased tail latency if you do not set an override.

Estimated mitigation ETA: our network team is targeting progressive restoration in eu-west at ~11:00 UTC and apac-edge by ~13:00 UTC, but we will post updates as we get confirmation.

If you want us to flip your org to an automatic reassignment we can do that (requires a one-line change on our control plane); reply and I will initiate.

Attachments: runbook-snapshot-20280630.pdf (short checklist), edge-peering-metrics-0900.png (live graph), temporary-traffic-override-commands.txt

Apologies for the disruption — we know how disruptive region-specific outages are and we are prioritizing a conservative failover to maintain correctness.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Li <ops@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud interruption in EU/APAC — immediate reassignment steps

On Fri, Jun 30, 2028 at 09:03, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick update from Redwood on the ongoing partition impacting our EU and APAC host pools...

Thanks Jordan — we’re seeing a spike in 503s across our EU tenants and a few failed job runs. Two quick questions:

- If we set X-Redwood-Region to us-west-2, will there be any data residency implications for our EU-only datasets? We have some models with restricted retention.
- Can Redwood push the override for our account rather than us changing many client instances? That would be faster for us.

If you can push the change, please confirm what rollback will look like so we can coordinate.

— Tom
Ops Lead, Acme Analytics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, CloudPartner Support <support@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud interruption in EU/APAC — immediate reassignment steps

Tom —

Short answers:

- Data residency: traffic routed to our US pools will be processed in the US; we will not replicate EU-only storage to US. If a workload requires EU-only persistence we will preserve the storage boundary and instead route only inference/compute to the US; this means for some jobs you may see latency for read/write operations that still hit EU storage. If you have strict EU legal constraints please reply and we’ll exclude those models from the override.

- Account-level override: we can apply a temporary traffic assignment on your account via the control plane immediately. This will add a per-account preference to route eligible inference sessions to us-west-2. ETA to apply: ~5 minutes after confirmation from you. Rollback: we’ll remove the preference and allow normal routing; to be extra safe we will roll back in staged steps (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% revert) and test with synthetic traffic.

Because this is a cross-region networking issue, we recommend the account-level override + the SDK flag if you can deploy it — the account-level override is a fast mitigation for customers who cannot change all clients quickly. I will kick this off for Acme upon your ok.

Action items for us (Redwood):
- Apply account-level traffic preference for Acme if you confirm (we’ll record the change and open a short maintenance note).
- Provide 1-hour post-incident log export to your ops mailbox (s3 link) including per-request region routing metadata and KV cache hit rates.
- Follow up with full timeline and RCA within 72 hours.

Please reply YES to confirm we should apply the override.

— Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Jul 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Cloud interruption in EU/APAC — internal notes and next steps

Folks — forwarding the thread with Acme. Summary and internal next steps so we have alignment before the customer postmortem: 

Incident summary:
- Start: 2028-06-30 08:40 UTC — partial peering flap affecting eu-west and apac-edge front-line connectivity.
- Customer impact: 503s and increased tail latency for EU/APAC routed sessions. US pools unimpaired.
- Immediate mitigation: Account-level override for Acme initiated on 2028-06-30 11:52 UTC (canary then full). SDK flag recommended for client upgrades.

What we’ve completed:
- Applied account preference for Acme (force-region: us-west-2) at 11:52 UTC; canary verification at 11:55 UTC.
- Delivered temporary logs link to acme-ops@s3 (private bucket) at 12:10 UTC.
- Notified CloudPartner to investigate peering fabric — they have an open ticket SUP-8234.

Open internal action items (owners):
- Network (Markus): coordinate with CloudPartner to get BGP flap evidence and confirm root cause; deliver first draft of network RCA by 2028-07-02 18:00 UTC.
- Product/Infra (Lauren): review runbook failures and update the regional-failover section (ensure account-level override runbook clearly steps rollback). Deliver updates by 2028-07-03 EOD.
- Customer Success (Vanessa): schedule a 30-minute post-incident review with Acme (preferred window Mon 07/03 14:00-16:00 UTC).
- Account Exec (Jordan): draft customer-facing summary and proposed credits (if requested); deliver to acme-ops and legal by 2028-07-03.

Notes and evidence attached: runbook-snapshot-20280630.pdf, edge-peering-metrics-0900.png, temporary-traffic-override-commands.txt. I’ll open a shared doc for the RCA — link in the metadata.

We should treat this as a priority RCA (network + control plane interaction). I’ll coordinate an Incident War Room if Markus thinks the CloudPartner timeline will stretch beyond 24 hours.

— Jordan
